newsitem.title: UK: London coffee futures drop below $2,000 level.
newsitem.headline: London coffee futures drop below $2,000 level.

text.p: London coffee futures retreated further on Thursday with front-month July falling below the closely-watched $2,000 per tonne level for the first time in almost three weeks.
This marked a reversal from a recent price rally which had propelled the futures for the robusta type of beans, traditionally used in making instant coffee, to a 20-month high last week.
The July contract fell to hit $1,995 briefly before standing at $2,000 per tonne at 1446 GMT, still down $83 on the day but substantially higher than this year's floor of $1,203.
Traders said the setback could be temporary and the market would swing up rapidly again if a frost were to hit the Brazilian crop over the next few weeks.

Coffee's rally this year was led by New York's futures market for arabica beans, the high quality coffee, due to the volatile mix of aggressive speculative buying, low roaster (processor) stocks, supply disruptions from Colombia and prospects of a lower Brazilian crop.
Roasters have replenished their low stocks as producers have shipped coffee heavily in recent weeks to take advantage of the steep prices.
